title: Old Furnace: Repair or Replace?
summary: Money Pit Q&A advising against replacing an old oil furnace with a heat pump because of cooler supply air; recommends a new oil furnace.

assertions.quote: Oil powered furnace air comes out at 140 degrees. With a heat pump, that temperature drops to about 110 degrees.
We suggest replacing the old oil fired furnace with new oil fired furnace, which will be much more efficient. Skip the heat pump.

verdicts.note: Oil is among the costliest heating fuels and heat pumps cut bills for nearly all oil-heated homes in national simulations.
In RMI's Providence model, heat pumps have a lower net present cost than heating-oil systems, as well as lower emissions.
